Glasgow is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable new boiler supply and installation services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Glasgow and the surrounding Glasgow City region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional boiler installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Glasgow City, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any new boiler supply and installation requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Glasgow with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: How long does a boiler installation take?
faqs.a: A straightforward like-for-like combi boiler swap takes 1-2 days. Moving the boiler location or converting from a heat-only system to a combi takes 2-4 days.

faqs.q: Do I need a combi boiler or a system boiler?
faqs.a: Combi boilers suit most homes up to 3 bedrooms with 1-2 bathrooms — no hot water tank needed. System boilers suit larger homes with higher hot water demand. Your installer should calculate your requirements before recommending.

faqs.q: What is the best boiler brand?
faqs.a: Worcester Bosch, Viessmann, and Vaillant consistently top reliability surveys. All three offer extended warranties of 8-12 years when installed by accredited engineers. Brand matters less than correct sizing and installation quality.

faqs.q: Do I need to notify anyone when a new boiler is installed?
faqs.a: Yes — your Gas Safe registered installer must notify Building Control within 30 days of installation under the Competent Person Scheme. You will receive a Building Regulations completion certificate.

localParagraph: Glasgow's diverse housing stock presents unique considerations for boiler installation, with properties ranging from Victorian tenements in areas like Dennistoun and Partick to post-war semis in Castlemilk and modern new-builds across the city's regenerated waterfront. As part of Scotland's largest city, Glasgow experiences mixed water hardness, meaning that neither heavily scaled pipework nor particularly soft water conditions dominate — though installers should still assess each property individually and consider whether a scale reducer or system filter is appropriate. The varied age of Glasgow's housing means that engineers frequently encounter outdated pipework, older radiator systems, and non-standard flue configurations, particularly in the West End's traditional tenement blocks or the stone-built terraces of Shawlands. Choosing a qualified Gas Safe registered installer with genuine experience across Glasgow's property mix is essential, as the correct boiler size and system design will depend heavily on the building's construction era, insulation levels, and existing heating infrastructure. A thorough survey before any installation is always advisable.
whatItInvolves: A new boiler installation involves removing your existing unit, upgrading the flue and pipework where required, fitting and commissioning the new boiler, and registering it with Building Control via the Competent Person Scheme. All new boiler installations must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer — it is illegal for anyone else to do this work.
process: Day 1: drain down the system, remove the old boiler, cap off existing connections. Upgrade the flue if required — most modern boilers use a concentric flue that vents through an external wall. Fit the new unit, connect flow and return pipes, gas supply, and condensate drain. Commission the boiler following manufacturer guidelines, balance the radiators, and register the installation. You'll receive a Building Regulations completion certificate within 28 days.
whatToExpect: A standard like-for-like boiler swap takes 1-2 days. A full system change — moving the boiler or converting from back boiler to combi — takes 2-4 days. Your new boiler should come with a manufacturer warranty of 5-12 years depending on brand. Always register the warranty within 30 days of installation.
